# scripts/Cinema/CineEditor.gd

[Source:1](../../../../../scripts/Cinema/CineEditor.gd#L1)

Declarations come from source. Unannotated types are explicit; see the [system guides](../../../../systems/README.md) for runtime schemas, nullability, ownership, units and side effects.

Scene-driven shot selection independent of level stories: observe long takes or drama event-driven cuts.
CineEvents drives interest; CineShot frames subjects, CineVantage tests placement/occlusion, and CineOperator moves the camera.
Pinned shots, minimum age, jump-cut rules, conversation continuity, crowding, and loss of subject govern cuts.
Scene dictionaries and event schemas are documented in docs/systems/cinematics.md.

Base: `Node`. Registered class: `none`.

### hold

```gdscript
func hold(held: bool) -> void
```

[Source:266](../../../../../scripts/Cinema/CineEditor.gd#L266)

Held: the camera is someone else's for now (flown, following a man); the
scene is kept and events still heard, and it takes up again as it was.
On hold: its slow motion over, any wipe gone, the camera's own lens back,
and nothing it hears slows or shakes anything. Taken up again, it forgets
what it heard meanwhile and takes a fresh shot of the scene as it is.

| Parameter | Type in source | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `held` | `bool` | required |

Return type: `void`.
